questions.q: Match each Kafka Streams abstraction to how it treats the records of its topic.
pairs: Each record is an insert: a repeated key adds another record
Each record is an update for its key, and a null value is a delete
Every instance holds the data of all the topic's partitions
questions.explain: A KStream is a record stream; a KTable is a changelog stream (upserts per key, null deletes); a GlobalKTable is filled from all partitions on every instance, so joins against it need no co-partitioning, at the cost of local storage and broker load.

questions.q: An instance running a stateful task fails, and the task moves to another instance with no standby replica. Put what happens in order, first to last.
items: The instance running the task fails
The task is assigned to another instance
The task restores its state store by replaying the store's changelog topic
The task starts processing records again
questions.explain: Each state store has a changelog topic. A task restarted on another machine restores its store by replaying the changelog before it processes; standby replicas keep copies elsewhere to cut that restore time.
